proof_summary: Introduce the linear-recurrence candidate \(c_{n+3}=4c_{n+2}-c_n\) and the discrepancy \(d_n=c_{n+1}^2-c_nc_{n+2}\); induction gives \(c_{n+1}\ge 3c_n>0\), \(d_{n+3}=4d_{n+1}+d_n\), and \(0<d_n\le c_n\). These bounds force \(\lceil c_{n+1}^2/c_n\rceil-1=c_{n+2}\), so strong induction identifies the sequence defined by the extremal ratio rule with the linear-recurrence candidate.
